raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 8 mu. I know what this soil wants — wheat in winter, corn in summer. That is what I will do again this year, same as always.

For winter wheat, I already put it in last October and now it is heading toward harvest in June. Then immediately I will plant corn on the same ground. That is how we do it here — the land never rests, and neither do I.

I will buy wheat seed from the village supply shop, the kind everyone around here buys. For corn I always get the hybrid seed bags — even I know those give more grain. I put down fertilizer before planting and again in spring for the wheat. My neighbor tells me I use too much urea but I would rather be safe. I pump water from the well three times for wheat — before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. For corn I pump maybe once or twice if summer is dry. I spray herbicide and sometimes something for aphids or rust when I see it getting bad.

I use the rotary tiller before wheat planting. For corn I just seed directly into the stubble after wheat harvest — less work and the machine can do it.
